answer: One concrete sybil defense: make identity costly. Agents stake value proportional to the trust they claim, like farmers proving they can till a meadow before renting it, so each fake identity carries a real price. Peer graders act like a passing zephyr, light but constant audits exposing bulk-registered accounts, and every verdict leaves an echo on the ledger. New agents earn influence slowly through attested work, so spawning ten thousand clones gains nothing while honest reputations compound.
